title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
layout_note: Two identical top-to-bottom pipelines side by side, pre-training on the left and fine-tuning on the right. The halves have no titles and no divider, only whitespace, and differ only in their example text and their data note.
grouping: No containers or background panels. Each half is one vertical spine (input text box, retriever, encoder, answer box) with its data sources hung off the right edge as coloured notes joined by dashed arrows, and a curved skip arrow on the left that carries the input past the retriever to an (x, z) label in front of the encoder. Colour families carry type: pale blue = the two learned modules, light grey with a dashed border = text instances (input and answer), yellow = the sampled training data (pre-training corpus, supervised data), green = the textual knowledge corpus.
shapes_depth: Flat 2-D, TikZ-like, no shadows. Modules are wide rounded rectangles with a thin blue outline and a pale blue fill. Text instances are square-cornered light-grey boxes with a dashed dark outline and a sans-serif label (Unlabeled text, Input query, Answer) on a white patch that breaks the top-left of the border. Corpora are document-like notes with one clipped corner and a darker olive outline. Example text is set in a typewriter face with [MASK] in red; every element carries a blue italic math symbol (x, y, theta, phi, calligraphic X and Z). Arrows are thin black with solid heads; links to the corpora are dashed and labelled in italics (sample, retrieve).
proposed_highlight: The paper's two components, Neural Knowledge Retriever (theta) and Knowledge-Augmented Encoder (phi), are the only solid rounded boxes and the only blue-filled shapes, placed on the central spine with their parameter symbols in blue italic; everything else is data (dashed grey boxes) or a source (coloured notes). Repeating both boxes unchanged in the right half shows they carry over from pre-training to fine-tuning.
lesson: Drawing pre-training and fine-tuning as two identical copies of one pipeline, changing only the example text and the data note, shows that the modules are shared without any arrow or label saying so.
notes: elements 'other' = the blue italic math symbols that tag every box and the (x, z) pair, and the clipped-corner document notes for the corpora. The pre-training and fine-tuning roles of the two halves come from the caption, not from any text in the drawing. Venue ICML as recorded (venue_source semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2002.08909).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: retrieval-augmented LM pretraining and open-domain QA

core.what: two identical top-down pipelines side by side, pre-training left and fine-tuning right: input text -> Neural Knowledge Retriever -> Knowledge-Augmented Encoder -> Answer, with a retrieved-from corpus note hung off the retriever's right and a sampled-from data note at the top right; only the data and the example text change

relations.form: each half is a vertical spine of straight down-arrows: grey dashed text box (x) -> pale-blue retriever (theta) -> pale-blue encoder (phi) -> grey dashed answer box (y)
a green folded-corner 'Textual knowledge corpus (Z)' note sits right of the retriever and a dashed arrow labeled 'retrieve' points from it into the retriever
a curved arrow from the input text and a short arrow from the retriever meet at a bare italic '(x, z)' label left of the spine, which then curves into the encoder
a yellow folded-corner note (Pre-training corpus X / Supervised data) at the top right sends a dashed 'sample' arrow curving into the input text box
inputs and answers are real typewriter examples: 'The [MASK] at the top of the pyramid' -> '[MASK] = pyramidion', 'what's the angle of an equilateral triangle?' -> '60 degrees'

channels.colour: fill = kind of element: pale blue = learned modules, grey with dashed border = text instances, yellow note = sampled training data, green note = knowledge corpus; red = the [MASK] token; blue italic = each element's symbol; one meaning each
channels.shape: rounded rectangles = learned modules, dashed-border boxes = text instances, folded-corner notes = data sources/corpora
channels.line: solid arrows = forward computation, dashed arrows = sampling from and retrieving from a corpus
channels.frame: no frames; the two halves are separated only by whitespace and carry no titles

quality.strengths: the two stages are identical pipelines placed side by side, so the reader sees one retrieve-then-encode architecture serving both; data is drawn as real examples with [MASK] in red; corpora are a distinct glyph beside the flow with their own dashed line style; colour and shape each carry one meaning; spines are straight
quality.weaknesses: the retrieved document z is never shown as text - only the bare '(x, z)' symbol in the margin - so what the encoder reads is hidden; the two halves have no titles saying pre-training vs fine-tuning; the (x, z) join is drawn as two curved arrows bending round the left edge; the retrieval as a latent variable and the backprop to the retriever are not drawn

insights.structure: Two identical vertical pipelines side by side (pre-training left, fine-tuning right) with no titles or divider, each a spine of input text, retriever, encoder and answer box with corpora hung off the right.
insights.data: Text instances are grey dashed-border boxes with real typewriter examples ([MASK] in red); learned modules are pale-blue rounded boxes; data sources are folded-corner notes, yellow for sampled training data and green for the knowledge corpus; every element carries a blue italic symbol (x, z, theta, phi, y).
insights.emphasis: Only the corpus notes and the example text change between halves, so the reader sees the same retrieve-then-encode architecture serves both stages.
insights.flow: Top to bottom down each spine; dashed arrows labelled 'sample' and 'retrieve' come in from the right-side notes, and a curved skip arrow on the left carries x past the retriever into an (x, z) pair.
insights.avoid: The two halves have no headings, so pre-training vs fine-tuning must be inferred from the example text and data notes.

arrangement.units: two unframed vertical pipelines separated by whitespace
arrangement.inputs_as: grey dashed text box with a real example sentence
arrangement.shared: same module boxes and green knowledge-corpus note in both halves
